title: Reliable Estimation of Differential Privacy under Selection Bias
abstract: arXiv:2610.27021v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Statistical privacy audits are essential for verifying the theoretical privacy guarantees of differentially private (DP) mechanisms. Auditors typically use Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) to estimate a lower bound on the true privacy leakage of DP mechanisms at a specified confidence level, which should not exceed the theoretical privacy upper bound guaranteed by DP. However, we found that many auditing implementations in prior work introduce a selection bias when running MIAs, which leads to statistically invalid and overestimated lower bounds. Because most audits are not tight, this bias has thus far gone unnoticed: the estimated lower bounds remained well below the theoretical upper bounds. Nevertheless, accurately evaluating this lower bound is critical, as a flawed statistical assessment could lead to false alarms on correct mechanisms or an incorrect evaluation of the guarantee's tightness. translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.27021v1 公告类型：交叉。摘要：统计隐私审计对于验证差分隐私（DP）机制的理论隐私保证至关重要。审计人员通常使用成员推断攻击（MIA）在指定置信水平下估计DP机制真实隐私泄露的下界，该下界不应超过DP所保证的理论隐私上界。然而，我们发现以往工作中的许多审计实现在运行MIA时引入了选择偏差，导致统计上无效且被高估的下界。由于大多数审计本身并不紧致，这种偏差至今未被察觉：估计出的下界仍远低于理论上界。尽管如此，准确评估这一下界至关重要，因为存在缺陷的统计评估可能导致对正确机制的误报，或对隐私保证紧致性的错误评估。本工作采用了来自统……（摘要不完整）
tldr: 本文揭示了以往差分隐私审计实现在运行成员推断攻击时引入选择偏差、从而产生统计上无效且被高估的隐私泄露下界这一问题，并提出了在选择偏差下可靠估计差分隐私的方法。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a selection bias in prior DP auditing implementations when running membership inference attacks—which yields statistically invalid and overestimated privacy leakage lower bounds—and proposes a reliable approach for estimating differential privacy under selection bias.
